result.summary: The food delivery home screen is largely well-structured, but several elements are clipped at the right edge of the viewport and one card's favorite button has inconsistent styling. The 'Trattoria Piccol...' card in the horizontal carousel is cut off mid-title without visible affordance, and the category chip row is also truncated. The second 'Popular right now' card is cropped by the bottom navigation bar, hiding its title and rating.

issues.description: The third card in the 'Fastest near you' carousel ('Trattoria Piccol...') is clipped by the right viewport edge, with the restaurant name truncated mid-word and no visible scroll indicator or fade to signal horizontal scrollability.
issues.suggestion: Add a peek/gutter offset so partially visible cards are clearly intentional, ellipsize the title properly, and add a gradient fade or scroll indicator to hint at horizontal scrolling.

issues.description: The second 'Popular right now' card (the -20% pizza) is cut off by the bottom navigation bar, hiding its name, rating, delivery time and price so the item cannot be evaluated without scrolling.
issues.suggestion: Add bottom padding equal to the nav bar height to the scroll container so cards are not obscured, and ensure card content is fully reachable.

issues.description: The two favorite (heart) buttons use inconsistent styling: the first has a white/light circular background with a dark outline heart, while the second has a dark circular background with a white heart.
issues.suggestion: Standardize the favorite button treatment across all cards (same background, icon color, and size) regardless of the underlying image.

issues.description: The category filter chip row is cut off at the right edge; a partially visible chip appears after 'Healthy' with no label readable.
issues.suggestion: Apply consistent horizontal padding and a peek offset or fade mask so partially visible chips look deliberate, and ensure the row is clearly scrollable.

issues.description: Secondary metadata text such as '€0.90 delivery' and '25–35 min • €0 delivery • Ramen' uses light grey on white, which may fall below the 4.5:1 contrast ratio.
issues.suggestion: Darken the secondary text color to meet WCAG AA contrast requirements.

issues.description: The notification bell with a red dot badge conveys unread state only by color/shape and likely has no accessible label or count.
issues.suggestion: Add an accessible label such as 'Notifications, 1 unread' and consider showing a numeric count.
